note: Everything the Orange Pi Zero 3 (4x A53 @ 1.5 GHz, 1.5 GB) is allowed to run, and what each thing may cost. CLAUDE.md rule 20: the board carries only what is real-time critical or must survive a WiFi loss or is wired to its own pins; everything that consumes the camera lives on the laptop. Nothing is added to the board without an entry here with a measured budget (pepin.census reads this file; ros/board.sh census compares it against a live ps). Budgets are today's measurement +50 % unless the entry's note says the number is a guess. The measurement is ps's %CPU, which is the process's average over its whole life, not an instant sample: read a census taken in the first minute after a start as start-up cost, not as the running cost (the census prints the age of the youngest process for that reason). Percentages are of ONE core: 400 % is the whole board. Census of 2026-09-14 12:40 EDT, stack up 2 min 22 s, nav:=true imu:=true tof:=true neck:=true side:=all, load 7.3.

ignore.why: kernel threads (kworker, SPRDWL/sdiohal for the WiFi-over-SDIO, ksoftirqd): no RSS, not started by us, not ours to budget. They do cost real CPU — the WiFi threads alone run 5-8 % — which is why the manifest promises well under 400 %.
the ssh session the census itself arrives on
the census's own ps and the shell around it (they read 300-400 % because they lived for a fraction of a second)
the ros2 CLI's discovery daemon, spawned by our own probes (ros/tools/topic_rate.py, flags.sh); idle between calls

processes.name: nav2_container
processes.role: Nav2 in one process: the AMCL-seat tracker's costmaps, the planner, the controller loop that drives the wheels, the behaviours and the behaviour tree (and a map server only when one is asked for).

components.name: map_server
components.role: serves a pgm (nav.launch.py map_server:=true, OFF by default: the one map is the tracker's live grid and its cache, and a file is only the seed of a room nobody has mapped)

components.name: planner_server
components.role: global path (absent when side=board: the laptop plans)

components.name: controller_server
components.role: the 8 Hz loop that turns a path into wheel speeds

components.name: bt_navigator
components.role: the behaviour tree that calls the rest

components.name: lifecycle_manager_navigation_all
components.role: brings those nodes up and bonds with them

processes.note: Measured 80 % / 101 MB with a goal running nothing — this is the idle cost of a stack that is merely alive. The single biggest consumer on the board and the reason nice 5 exists: the sensors must not wait for the planner.

processes.name: sensors_container
processes.role: The sensing half in one process at high priority: the lidar driver, the hull filter that makes /scan, the wheel bridge and the static sensor transforms.

components.name: scan_filter
components.role: cuts the cart's own hull out of the scan and republishes /scan

components.name: base_bridge
components.role: wheel speeds and odometry over TCP 3336, /cmd_vel in, /odom out, and the MPU6050's yaw rate as imu/data_raw whose zero is re-measured from the rest the wheels witness (C++ build when base_bridge_cpp:=true, else its own Python process)

components.name: base_to_imu
components.role: static base_link -> imu_link from config/imu.json (imu:=true only)

processes.note: Measured 21 % / 60 MB. ps sees the container, never the components: a component's own cost can only be read from the node's rate, not from this table.

processes.name: relocalizer
processes.role: Scan-matching pose tracker and kidnapped-robot recovery, and the ONE owner of map -> odom in every situation: matches /scan against the map RTAB-Map's graph publishes (or, with nothing live, the board's own cache of it), republishes that map as /map_tracked for the costmaps, and searches the whole map when the fit dies.
processes.note: Measured 60 % / 80 MB standing still; a whole-map search is a burst well above that and short. 'sometimes' since 2026-09-22, when the board became odometry only and the map localiser a mode rather than the default: four A53 cores do not hold the tracker AND the laser odometry that replaces what it gave the EKF (90 % + 20 %), and 1.5 GB does not hold both either. Absent is IDLE now, not MISSING; running, it is measured against this budget exactly as before.

processes.name: run_recorder
processes.role: Writes every drive to disk (scans, odometry, pose, cmd_vel, camera): any run may be the one worth showing.
processes.note: Measured 16 % / 62 MB while idle (subscribed, nothing driving).

processes.name: tof_bridge
processes.role: Publishes the three VL53L1X ranges from the ToF server as ROS Range messages for Nav2's contact layer.
processes.note: Measured 13 % / 68 MB. An rclpy process costs ~65 MB before it does anything. The tf_gate of 2026-09-21 put an rclpy TF listener in here and took it to 20-37 % of a core; it came out on 2026-09-22 (the whiskers reach Nav2 as scan fans instead), so the next census should read 13 % again.

processes.name: laser_odometry
processes.role: Laser odometry: matches each LD19 scan against the one before it (rf2o, scan to scan, no map) and publishes /odom_laser, which the EKF fuses as a twist (odom3). The one odometry input a wheel spinning on carpet cannot fool.
processes.owner: pepin-ros.service -> ros/pepin_bringup/launch/robot.launch.py (laser_odom:=true, respawn, ghost wait, nice -5)
processes.note: TO MEASURE: every number here is an estimate and the first census after this feature lands replaces it. Where it comes from: RF2O's paper reports 0.9 ms per scan on one desktop core at 1080 beams; ours are 455, and an A53 at 1.5 GHz with no tuned SIMD is taken at 10x a desktop core, so 4-8 ms of the 100 ms between scans -> 4-8 %, +50 % -> 12, rounded to 20 because nothing is measured. The memory is a C++ ROS node's measured 28 MB (ekf_node) plus the ~40 MB of zenoh session every process on this board carries, and the same headroom. If the census says OVER, the honest lever is the node's freq, not this number.

processes.name: neck_state
processes.role: Reads the neck's encoders and publishes /neck/state and, behind its neck_tf flag, the live base_link -> camera_link.
processes.note: Measured 10 % / 66 MB.

processes.name: ekf_node
processes.role: Fuses the wheels and the gyro in the plane and owns odom -> base_link (the wheels over-report rotation on carpet, the gyro does not).
processes.owner: pepin-ros.service -> ros/pepin_bringup/launch/robot.launch.py (imu:=true and base_bridge_cpp:=true), ros/params/ekf.yaml, nice -5
processes.note: Measured 9 % / 28 MB.

processes.name: goal_server
processes.role: Takes goals on a socket so ordering a drive costs a socket write instead of a client boot; keeps the places book of the map in use.
processes.note: Measured 7 % / 76 MB. Moves to the laptop when side=laptop.

processes.name: ros2_launch
processes.role: The launch process itself: it started every ROS node above and respawns the ones that may come back alone.
processes.note: Measured 7 % / 70 MB. One launch process for sensors and Nav2 together, on purpose: two cost ~110 MB of Python each.

processes.name: zenoh_bridge
processes.role: The board's ROS graph over one TCP link to the laptop: only the topics the split needs cross.
processes.note: Measured 12 % / 52 MB for the pair: the bridge itself is 11 % / 23 MB and the `docker run` supervisor that holds it is ~1 % / 29 MB — the same regex claims both, because killing one kills the other. Runs only when PEPIN_SIDE=board or PEPIN_BRIDGE=on, but by then it is part of every drive, so it is expected whenever it is configured; a census with no bridge running is not red on its own (see `when`).

processes.name: zenoh_router
processes.role: The board's half of the rmw_zenoh transport (PEPIN_RMW=zenoh): the one process that carries this board's graph to the laptop's router. Board-internal traffic does NOT pass through it — every node here is a zenoh peer of every other over the host loopback (measured 0.0 % router CPU for a 10 Hz x 100 kB board-internal flow, against 1.4 % with the same two nodes as clients).

processes.name: base_server
processes.role: The wheels next to the UART: speed commands, odometry ticks and the deadman, on TCP 3336. The last thing between a runaway and a stopped cart.
processes.note: Measured 10 % / 18 MB. Outside Docker on purpose: it must survive a container restart.

processes.name: tof_server
processes.role: Streams the three VL53L1X ranges over TCP 3335 from the I2C bus.
processes.owner: pepin-tof.service (/opt/pepin, systemd; tof-init.service re-addresses the sensors first)
processes.note: Measured 9 % / 15 MB.

processes.name: ser2net
processes.role: The servo bus and the lidar as TCP ports (3333/3334) so the laptop's tools can reach them without a serial cable.
processes.note: Measured 4 % / 3 MB.

processes.name: ustreamer
processes.role: The overview camera as MJPEG on http 8080: the one camera consumer that stays on the board, because it only copies frames out of the USB stack and never decodes them.
processes.owner: pepin-camera.service (on the board only; the unit is not yet in board/)
processes.note: Measured 2 % / 13 MB at 1280x720, 15 fps, --drop-same-frames 30. The image is passed through, not encoded; anything that LOOKS at these frames (depth, scans, matching) belongs on the laptop — rule 20.

processes.name: docker
processes.role: The container runtime and one supervisor per container: what keeps pepin-ros and the bridge alive across a crash.
processes.note: Measured ~1 % total and ~150 MB across dockerd, containerd, two shims and the pepin-ros `docker run`. Memory, not CPU, is what it costs us.

processes.name: reap_ros2_cli
processes.role: Every minute, kills ros2 CLI tools older than 90 s left inside the container — a dozen leftovers took the board to load 12 on 2026-09-13.
processes.note: A guess: the oneshot lives under a second and a census almost never catches it. Its point is that it is cheap and that a census that DOES catch it should not go red.

processes.name: session_logger
processes.role: The per-drive recorder started by ros/goto.sh, ros/tour.sh and ros/teleop.sh: scans, odometry, pose and commands into one jsonl for the post-drive plots.
processes.owner: started inside the pepin-ros container by ros/goto.sh:95, ros/tour.sh:26, ros/teleop.sh:32 (ros/tools/session_logger.py)
processes.note: A guess: it has never been measured on its own, and it only runs during a drive, which is when the board is busiest. Measure it on the next recorded drive and replace this number.

processes.name: slam_frame
processes.role: RETIRED (World R, 2026-09-19), off by default and kept reachable by CLAUDE.md rule 19: broadcasts the laptop's RTAB-Map correction as map -> odom instead of the tracker, from /map_odom.
processes.note: A guess from the other small rclpy nodes, and it will stay one: this node runs only with nav.launch.py's slam:=true (the board's PEPIN_SLAM), never together with the relocalizer, which owns map -> odom in every situation the stack ships with. No census has caught it.

processes.name: link_watch
processes.role: In the thin-client split, watches the link to the laptop and stops the cart when the planner half goes away.
processes.owner: pepin-ros.service -> ros/pepin_bringup/launch/nav.launch.py (side=board, no respawn: its exit is the signal)
processes.note: A guess from the other small rclpy nodes; it runs only when side=board.

processes.name: foxglove_bridge
processes.role: The Foxglove websocket. Being removed: the laptop reads the board through the zenoh bridge, and a second serialiser of every topic is a luxury on four A53 cores.
processes.owner: a component of sensors_container behind foxglove:=true, which defaults to false since 2026-09-14 (ros/pepin_bringup/launch/robot.launch.py)
processes.note: Not expected on the board any more: the laptop runs one Foxglove bridge and it sees the board through the zenoh bridge. If a process with this name appears, someone passed foxglove:=true. As a component inside sensors_container it is invisible to ps — the census cannot prove its absence, only catch it as a standalone process. Check the launch argument, not this line.
